common_name: Red Diamond Loropetalum (Candy-Red Burgundy-Leaf Fringe Flower)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring in well-drained, moderately fertile, slightly acidic soil in full sun to partial shade; full sun brings out the deepest foliage color and the heaviest bloom.

directions: Grow Red Diamond in acidic, humus-rich, well-drained soil, watering deeply through the first year to establish a strong root system before easing off. Its year-round burgundy-purple foliage sets off candy-red spring flowers described as the deepest red among loropetalum cultivars, with sporadic rebloom from early summer into fall. Prune to shape immediately after the main spring flush, since later cuts remove developing flower buds; avoid tight shearing, which spoils the naturally mounded form. Space plants generously for hedging so mature specimens can fill in without constant crowding pressure.

common_name: China Pink Loropetalum (Soft Pink Burgundy-Leaf Fringe Flower)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring in humus-rich, free-draining, acidic soil in full sun to partial shade with some direct sun for best bloom and color.

directions: China Pink forms a dense, rounded evergreen mound with burgundy-purple foliage that holds its color through the seasons, punctuated in spring by a heavy flush of soft pink, tassel-like flowers with some repeat bloom later on. Plant in free-draining, organically rich soil kept on the acidic side, avoiding lime, and water regularly the first season to establish before tapering to a more drought-tolerant routine. A position with morning or afternoon direct sun keeps foliage color richest and blooms most abundant compared with deep shade. Its dense, full habit suits hedging and screening as well as specimen use in mixed borders.

common_name: Plum Delight Loropetalum (Rose-Purple Dark Pink Fringe Flower)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring in acidic, well-drained soil in full sun to partial shade; full sun deepens foliage color and thickens the spring bloom.

directions: Plum Delight is a vigorous, fast-growing selection whose oval leaves emerge rosy-purple and mature to a black-purple to deep burgundy that holds well into the growing season, contrasted by large dark pink flowers in mid-spring. Grow in acidic, well-drained soil in full sun to partial shade, watering deeply through the establishment year and less often once roots are settled. Because it grows quickly and can reach small-tree proportions, plan on pruning right after the spring bloom to control size and maintain a dense hedge or screen rather than waiting until growth gets out of hand. Avoid shearing into tight geometric shapes, which sacrifices next year's flower buds and the plant's naturally graceful, arching silhouette.

common_name: Pizazz Loropetalum (Compact Dark Purple Plum-Flowered Fringe Flower)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring in rich, humusy, acidic, well-drained soil in full sun to partial shade, giving at least 4-6 hours of direct sun for best color.

directions: Pizazz stays notably more compact than many rubrum loropetalums, with burgundy-green new growth maturing to dark purple foliage and a spring flush of plum-colored fringe flowers. Site it in rich, humusy, acidic soil with good drainage, watering consistently the first season and only occasionally afterward once it is established. Its tidy, slow-to-medium growth habit needs little pruning to stay dense, making it a good choice for foundation plantings or low hedges where larger cultivars would quickly outgrow the space. Trim lightly right after flowering if needed, since pruning later in the season removes wood that would otherwise set next spring's blooms.

common_name: Razzle Dazzle Loropetalum (Bright Pink Burgundy-Green Fringe Flower)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring in rich, humusy, acidic, well-drained soil in partial sun to partial shade.

directions: Razzle Dazzle carries light to dark burgundy foliage that can shade toward green-burgundy depending on light exposure, with a heavy spring show of bright pink, tassel-like flowers on a rounded, variably sized habit. Plant in rich, humusy, acidic, well-drained soil and water regularly through establishment, since consistent moisture keeps the foliage from scorching in hotter Gulf Coast summers. It tolerates more shade than many loropetalum selections, though flowering is fullest with some direct morning or afternoon sun. Prune immediately after the spring flowering flush to manage its size and keep the habit rounded rather than open and leggy.
